title: Explore Integers and Their Opposites
objective: I can use integers to represent quantities in everyday life, explain what 0 means in each situation, and name the opposite of an integer on the number line.
model: number line with 0 as the chosen starting level; an integer and its opposite sit the same distance from 0 on opposite sides

widgets.where: Practice §1 items 1.1-1.4 (mc, num; 1.1 with number-line figure)
widgets.component: reading a number line, moving left, distance between 3 and 11, equal distance from 5
widgets.root: Figure 1.1 plots A=3, B=5, C=7, D=9 so key C is right. All four use only whole-number distance on a 0-10 line, the prerequisite for opposites.

widgets.component: −86 m below sea level, opposite of −9, opposite of 0
widgets.root: Keys −86, 9, 0 verified; 2.3's distractors target 'zero has no opposite' and '−0'.
Each situation names its own zero; matches the objective's 'what 0 means'.

widgets.component: opposite of −7 'stays negative'; opposite of −12°C written −24
widgets.root: e=1 in both lands on the student-thinking line; fixes give 7 and 12.
Comparing and ordering integers is the objective of 7-4 (Compare and Order Integers and Rational Numbers), not of 7-1, which stops at representing quantities and naming opposites.
widgets.replacement: Replace with a number-line task in the lesson's own idea: 'Which pair are opposites on the number line?' using −8, 8, −3, 3 plotted on a figure, so the student names opposites by distance from 0 and not by order.

widgets.component: farther below sea level than −86 (−120), table of integer → opposite (−15, 8, 0, −100), statement about 0
widgets.root: 3.2 asks only about depth beyond a given depth, which is the meaning of the negative sign; 3.5's key (0 is an integer, neither positive nor negative, its own opposite) is right.

widgets.component: opposite of −19 and 'loss of 24 yards: which integer for the opposite situation'
widgets.root: Sampled; checks agree; typographic minus used.

widgets.where: Practice §4 items 4.5-4.6 and Challenge §1 items 1.3-1.4 (gen:integerOpposites L3, number-line figure)
widgets.component: 'Point W shows 7. Which point shows its opposite?' beside a figure
widgets.root: The stem names the tick index while the figure plots tick × unit: I rendered L3 over 600 seeds and in 103 (about 17%) the stem number disagrees with the plotted point (for example stem 'Point W shows 7' with W plotted at 35 on a line stepping by 5; 'Point L shows −7' with L at −14). The key follows the figure, so a student who reads the stem finds the 'right' answer is the opposite of a different number.
widgets.replacement: In assets/studio-gen/coordinate.js oppLetters(), the stem prints o.show(t) (the tick index k) while the figure plots the point at k × unit. Print o.show(t × unit) in the stem (and the 'Its opposite is …' explanation), or force unit = 1 for this item; then add to tools/studio-gen.test.mjs an assertion that the number in a 'Point X shows N' stem equals the plotted value of X over 300 seeds.

widgets.component: manipulable number line: drag/tap the opposite of a given point
widgets.root: The lesson's model made manipulable (assets/studio-act/nline.js): grading names the wrong-side and one-tick-off errors.

widgets.component: 3-yard loss is −3, situation for −15, opposite of −63, crate 7 m below the dock
widgets.root: Keys verified; each stem is self-contained.

widgets.component: net result of −10, 4, −3, 21 (12 yards gained) and 'what does 0 represent in this football situation'
widgets.root: 5.2 needs adding signed integers; no lesson in Grade 6 units 2-9 teaches integer addition (7-1 to 7-9 are opposites, number line, absolute value, order, coordinate plane). 5.3 also lost the football scenario, so 'this football situation' points at nothing.
widgets.replacement: 5.2: 'In one series a team had a 10-yard loss, a 4-yard gain, a 3-yard loss and a 21-yard gain. Which list writes the four plays as integers with the line of scrimmage as 0?' choices '−10, 4, −3, 21' (key), '10, 4, 3, 21', '−10, −4, −3, −21', '10, −4, 3, −21'. 5.3: 'In a football series the line of scrimmage is 0. What does 0 represent?' with the existing choices.
